high.title: Expert: VN-Index Will Soon Reach 2,000 Points
high.summary: VN-Index has just established a new historical high, but market euphoria is not spreading as strongly as previous breakouts. Trading liquidity has not truly exploded, foreign investors continue net selling, while money flow continuously rotates between large-cap groups. According to Pinetree Securities analyst Nguyen Tan Phong, last week marked an important milestone when VN-Index officially set a new historical high at 1,925 points, surpassing the old record of 1,918 points. The most notable point is the clear change in money flow structure. After an extended hot streak, Vingroup stocks began to consolidate and money gradually spread to other sectors, especially banking with stocks like VPB, VCB, BID, ACB, and TPB rising positively. The oil & gas group with GAS and BSR also gained momentum. This rotation suggests the market is entering a more selective phase where stock picking will be crucial rather than simply following the index.

high.title: Bad Debt at Many Banks Rises Sharply: Two Banks Have Bad Debt Balance Exceeding 40,000 Billion VND
high.summary: According to financial reports from 27 listed banks, total bad debt as of March 31, 2026 reached 292,160 billion VND, increasing by 28,065 billion VND compared to end-2025, equivalent to 11% growth. Notably, most banks recorded an upward trend. Among 27 surveyed banks, only three banks recorded declining bad debt: VietinBank, NamABank, and ABBank. In terms of absolute scale, BIDV currently has the largest bad debt in the system at 42,655 billion VND, increasing by 7,678 billion VND in Q1, equivalent to 22% growth. This rising trend in banking sector NPLs could signal credit quality concerns and may impact monetary policy decisions and banking sector stability going forward.

high.title: Banks May Soon Have Tens of Thousands of Billions More VND for Lending?
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam is seeking comments on a draft circular amending Circular 22/2019 on safety limits and ratios for banking activities. The draft stipulates excluding 80% of State Treasury term deposits from mobilization calculations, meaning 20% of State Treasury term deposits will be included in the denominator when calculating the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR). This is a significant change from current regulations that exclude 100% of State Treasury term deposits. Expert Nguyen Danh Thai from CKG Vietnam notes this will particularly benefit state-owned commercial banks due to their large State Treasury deposit volumes, helping reduce pressure to mobilize retail and corporate deposits to meet safety ratios. Deposit rates could cool further as banks no longer need to "race" to increase input rates to balance credit growth.

medium.title: Bill Gates Foundation Sells All Microsoft Shares But Still Pours Money Into Vietnamese Securities
medium.summary: Gates Foundation Trust sold all remaining 7.7 million Microsoft shares in Q1/2026, worth about $3.2 billion, but continues to maintain investments in Vietnamese stocks through Vietnam Enterprise Investments Limited (VEIL) managed by Dragon Capital. This demonstrates continued foreign institutional confidence in Vietnamese equity markets despite global portfolio rebalancing.

medium.title: Dragon Capital Securities Director Names Stock Groups Being "Forgotten" While VN-Index Peaks
medium.summary: Dragon Capital's Vo Nguyen Khoa Tuan suggests that while Vingroup stocks dominate market attention, other sectors with strong fundamentals but attractive valuations are being overlooked. He views the 5-10x price increases in Vingroup stocks over 8 years as reasonable given the company's operational intensity, while highlighting opportunities in undervalued sectors.

medium.title: Amid VN-Index Records, Agriseco Names 5 Companies With Notable High Dividend Yields
medium.summary: Agriseco Research recommends five dividend-focused stocks for 2026: BMP, MSH, SCS, SMB, and QTP. These companies offer high expected dividend yields, relatively healthy financial foundations, and reasonable valuations, providing an alternative strategy during market differentiation when index leaders may carry chase risks.

medium.title: Holding Over 99% of Treasury Deposits, Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV and Agribank Benefit Most From New State Bank Regulations
medium.summary: The new regulation allowing banks to include 20% of State Treasury term deposits in their mobilization base primarily benefits Big4 state-owned banks, as they hold nearly all Treasury deposits in the system. As of end-March, State Treasury deposits reached approximately 650,000 billion VND, with Big4 banks controlling over 99% of this amount.
